**Copying damaged rows.** An existing row with a damaged body and retained version stays in backup as `{key, items: null, index, unreadable: true}`, where `index` is its exact nonempty version; the existing key order and coherent copy header remain. This is separate from import/restore refusing unreadable input under N4. A lost version requires the P/01.1 R028 log entry, a nonzero backup CLI exit and preservation of the previous published file. HTTP copy may return `503 UnavailableFault` before `200` or close incompletely after `200`; a completed copy that omits the row or invents its `index` is invalid. An import refusal of unreadable input does not permit omitting a damaged row from backup. The `spoil-row` binding uses `what=body` or `what=index`; without it the dependent observation stays `NotExecuted`.

For the bindings of the target `P/01/production` the words of the payload mean the following. The boundary `admission_time` is the wall clock of the daemon process that P/01.1 N3 «Admission time» reads at admission: the provider observes this clock domain of the process, and the admission time that the daemon stores is judged by the public outcomes of the case, not by the provider. The resource `heap` is the resident anonymous memory of the process (`RssAnon` of `/proc/<pid>/status`), and `memory` is its resident set (`VmRSS`); a heap figure of a language runtime is no resource of the form. With the latch `sink` the provider is the reader of the output, and `cancel` is its deactivation: the provider closes the sink at `deactivate`, the `monotonic_ns` of the deactivation record is that moment, and no observation carries `cancel`. The phase `recover_mark` names no file: the mark is the first changing step of `recover` in `-dir` (P/01.3 R021), and the point of the fault is the first change of `-dir` after the first top-level entry that `recover` completes, so neither the payload nor the invocation carries a name of the mark. The phase `copy_after_headers` is the end of the stream as the client receives it after the complete header block of a `200`, made between the daemon and the client: it gives the half of `RUN-H03` that the CLI judges. The half of the daemon after `200`, only an incomplete close and no second fault, is judged on its own stream under the cancellation, the stalled sink and the stop that the judge makes; a failure inside the daemon has no binding.

Before measurement record exact Source/implementation/runner/profile/artifact/fixture/library/compiler identities, invocation and durability mode. Declare workload cardinalities, operation rate/mix, key/item/body sizes, replay locality, checkpoint policy, concurrency and input bytes; record CPU, RAM, storage/filesystem/mount/cache facts relevant to the experiment. The [first approved budgets](#first-approved-budgets) apply to the envelope named there. Cache/eligible-GC, output and cancellation budgets are not approved yet. Each of them, like the budgets of P/01.3 R035 and R036, is a finite positive budget declared by the implementation, and the probe of a dependent case receives its value as input from the environment (ADR-0130 Addendum (5) item 3). The implementation declares the value; the threshold of production acceptance is approved as in ADR-0130 Addendum (9), and a claim of the candidate alone is not enough (ADR-0130 Addendum (15) item 7). The stop budget fits below the actual manager stop deadline with measured teardown margin. Calibrate monotonic resolution/scheduling uncertainty separately; it does not increase a protocol budget. Candidate assertions alone do not qualify these inputs. Unknown values stay unknown, not invented universal defaults.

Test the two edges independently with distinct successful later applications; do not invent a counting rule from unadmitted requests, admitted refusals or replays. The age runs from the first application on the admission-time clock (R141). GC is finite only under the qualified workload/budget. Logical reclaim is not immediate physical file shrink.

The checks of P/01.1 R013 are the actual spread between the clocks beyond `CLOCK_SKEW`, a common shift and return, and the non-decrease of admission time. The probes also need a leader change, a Raft snapshot, the equality of admission time, and a replay held after `not_after` before the first application. Writer and client clocks belong to the scope only when the selected workload actually uses them; live P/03, P/04 or new N−1 stands are not assumed. Until the public case payload and a qualified provider exist, a dependent check stays `MissingBinding`/`NOTEXEC`.

Separate actual protocol output/state/replay from test-only instrumentation. Qualify each storage/clock/progress/fault binding independently with activated-stage receipts and negative controls; do not infer physical durability from ordinary process restart or SIGKILL. Complete recoverable bytes must be proved before judging the R144 ambiguous_barrier branch. Compare whole batch/id state, and admission metadata separately. An absent binding is not proof that an implementation is wrong or successful.

**Raw paths and route matching.** The shared P/01.1 R050 drain counts raw HTTP-stream bytes and its absolute monotonic interval starts after the complete refusal has been sent; chunked discard does not wait for a terminal chunk. This parsing reference does not replace the resource's own timeout outcomes or budgets with P/01 input-phase refusals, and adds no common response deadline to resource streams.

**Early refusal.** Follow P/01.1 R050: send the complete refusal with `Connection: close` first, then discard raw HTTP-stream bytes without parsing/execution, bounded by the declared length when framing supplies one, the declared raw-byte limit and the absolute monotonic drain deadline. The interval starts after the complete refusal is sent; a trickle does not extend it and chunked discard does not wait for a terminal chunk. Then close; add no second refusal or executed pipelined request. The console ([P/06.5](../../06-console/spec/06.5-console.norms.md)), its bytes door (P/06.1) and the resource (P/05) keep their own outcomes and declared limits. This reference does not copy P/01 input-timeout responses/budgets onto them: console slow-body `408` and BODY_WAIT from headers remain owned here; forwarding, pass and stream response budgets are not replaced by a common P/01 response deadline.
